lessons.title: Modals of deduction, passive and causative
lessons.programRef: Tle — Anglais : modaux, voix passive, causatif (à vérifier sur le texte officiel)
lessons.author: CastBridge (brouillon IA)
lessons.source: Rédaction originale ; textes d'exemple écrits pour CastBridge ; à relire par un enseignant
objectives: Exprimer la déduction avec must, can't, may, might.
Employer les modaux au passé (should have, needn't have).
Former la voix passive à tous les temps.
Utiliser le causatif have/get something done.
reviewNotes: Niveau d'avancement du passif impersonnel et du causatif (get + to infinitif) : à confronter au programme officiel de Tle A, C, D.
La différence entre needn't have et didn't need to varie selon les grammaires : à confirmer.
Dans l'exercice mod-06 question b, le QCM est volontairement simple ; un enseignant pourra le reformuler.

blocks.title: Modaux de déduction
blocks.md:
On emploie des modaux pour **déduire** ou supposer quelque chose, selon le degré de certitude : **must** (presque certain), **can't / couldn't** (presque certain que non), **may / might / could** (possible).
Présent : *He must be tired.* Passé : **modal + have + participe passé** : *He must have left.* En cours : *She must be working.*

items.text: must : I am sure it is true
can't : I am sure it is false

blocks.caption: Échelle de certitude : de must à can't.
blocks.alt: Une flèche verticale de 100 % à 0 % ; quatre cadres : must (sûr que c'est vrai), should (probable), may, might, could (possible), can't (sûr que c'est faux).

blocks.title: Déduction : présent et passé
blocks.md:
- *She **must** be at home : her light is on.*
- *He **can't** be serious !*
- *They **might** be late : the road is blocked.*
- *Someone **must have** taken my pen.* (je suis presque sûr)
- *He **can't have** left : his bag is still here.*
- *She **may/might/could have** missed the bus.* (possible)

Pour une certitude négative, on emploie **can't**, jamais *mustn't* (qui exprime l'interdiction).

blocks.title: Autres valeurs au passé
blocks.md:
- **Should have / ought to have + pp** : reproche ou regret : *You should have called me.*
- **Needn't have + pp** : c'était inutile, mais cela a été fait : *I needn't have hurried.*
- **Didn't need to** : c'était inutile, donc non fait (ou on ne sait pas).
- **Could have + pp** : possibilité non réalisée : *You could have won.*
- **Was able to** : capacité réalisée une fois ; *could* pour la capacité générale.

blocks.title: La voix passive
blocks.md:
**Forme** : be (au temps voulu) + participe passé : *The bridge was built in 1999. The letter has been sent. The road is being repaired.*
**Avec modal** : *It must be done. It must have been done.*
**Deux compléments** : *He was given a prize.* ; *A prize was given to him.*
L'**agent** (by…) n'est exprimé que s'il est utile. Seuls les verbes **transitifs** ont un passif.

blocks.title: Passif impersonnel (reporting verbs)
blocks.md:
Avec *say, believe, think, report, expect, know* : *It is said that he is rich.* ou *He is said to be rich.* Pour le passé : *He is said to have left.* (infinitif parfait).

Verbes qui ne se mettent pas au passif : les intransitifs (*arrive, happen, die*) et certains statifs (*have* au sens de posséder, *fit, suit*).

blocks.title: Le causatif
blocks.md:
**have / get + objet + participe passé** : faire faire un service : *I had my car repaired. She got her hair cut.* Parfois pour un malheur : *He had his bag stolen.*
**have + objet + infinitif sans to** : *The teacher had the students clean the board.*
**get + objet + to + infinitif** : *I got him to help me.*
**make + objet + infinitif sans to** (obliger) ; **let** (permettre) : *She made me wait. They let us go.*

blocks.title: Résoudre un exercice de modaux ou de voix
blocks.md:
1. **Déduction** : quel degré de certitude ? Présent ou passé ?
2. **Passif** : repérer le temps du verbe actif, mettre *be* à ce temps, ajouter le participe passé.
3. **Causatif** : qui fait l'action ? Si c'est quelqu'un d'autre pour un service, *have/get + objet + pp*.
4. Relire : le sens et la grammaire doivent s'accorder.

blocks.title: Exemple 1 : déduction
blocks.statement: Complete with a modal: 1) The lights are off and the car is gone, so they ______ be at home. 2) She ______ have forgotten : she always remembers. 3) He ______ be at the market : I'm not sure.

steps.md: **1)** Lumières éteintes et voiture partie : on est presque sûr qu'ils ne sont pas là : *can't be*.
**2)** « she always remembers » rend l'oubli presque impossible : *can't have forgotten*.
**3)** « I'm not sure » : *may/might be* au présent.

blocks.title: Exemple 2 : passif et causatif
blocks.statement: Rewrite: 1) They are building a new school. (passive) 2) Someone repaired my phone yesterday. (causative) 3) People believe that he is honest. (It is …)

steps.md: **1)** Present continuous actif → passif : *A new school is being built.*
**2)** On veut dire que l'on a fait réparer son téléphone : *I had my phone repaired yesterday.*
**3)** *It is believed that he is honest.* (ou *He is believed to be honest.*)

blocks.answer: 1) A new school is being built. 2) I had my phone repaired yesterday. 3) It is believed that he is honest.

blocks.title: Les pièges des modaux et du passif
blocks.md:
- **Mustn't** (interdiction) ≠ **can't** (déduction négative).
- **Must + have + pp** pour le passé : *He must have left*, non *He must left*.
- **Needn't have** ≠ **didn't need to**.
- Passif au present continuous : *is being repaired*, non *is repaired*.
- Causatif : *I had repaired my car* (faux sens) ≠ *I had my car repaired*.
- *By* + agent inutile (par exemple *by people*).

items: Écrire cinq phrases de déduction à partir de ce que vous voyez dans la salle de classe.
Mettre le dernier texte lu en classe au passif.

exercises.prompt: Associez chaque phrase à sa valeur.
pairs: Déduction passée négative : presque certain que non
exercises.explanation: Distinguer degré de certitude, reproche, inutilité et interdiction évite les contresens.
Present continuous passif : *is being + participe passé*.

exercises.prompt: True or false: « I had repaired my phone » means that someone else repaired it for me.
exercises.explanation: Faux. *I had repaired my phone* est un past perfect actif (j'avais réparé). Pour le causatif : *I had my phone repaired*.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite: 1) People say the minister is ill. (He is …) 2) A thief stole his bag. (He had …) 3) We have to finish the report today. (It must …) 4) I'm sure Paul didn't take it. (can't …) 5) It was unnecessary for you to come. (needn't …)
exercises.model: 1) He is said to be ill. 2) He had his bag stolen. 3) It must be finished today (The report must be finished today). 4) Paul can't have taken it. 5) You needn't have come.
exercises.explanation: Chaque transformation applique une structure précise : passif impersonnel, causatif, déduction passée, inutilité passée.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite in the passive, keeping the same tense: 1) They have repaired the bridge. 2) They are cleaning the market. 3) Somebody should have told him. 4) The headmaster will announce the results. 5) They gave Mary a scholarship.
exercises.model: 1) The bridge has been repaired. 2) The market is being cleaned. 3) He should have been told. 4) The results will be announced (by the headmaster). 5) Mary was given a scholarship (A scholarship was given to Mary).
rubric: Futur et deux compléments passifs (1 point).
exercises.explanation: On garde le temps du verbe actif et on le met à la forme « be + participe passé ».

exercises.prompt: Read: « Last night someone broke into Ms Ngo's shop. Nothing was taken, but the door was damaged. The owner is not at home. »

parts.prompt: Choose the best deduction: « The thief ____ in a hurry. »
parts.explanation: Preuve : rien n'a été pris. La déduction raisonnable sur le passé : *must have been*.

choices: The case is investigating at the moment.
The case has being investigated at the moment.
The case is being investigated at the moment.
The case investigates being at the moment.
parts.explanation: Present continuous passif : *is being + participe passé*. Les autres formes mélangent actif et passif.

parts.prompt: Ms Ngo wants a new door. Write a sentence with the causative.
parts.model: She is going to have a new door installed (by a carpenter).
parts.explanation: Le causatif exprime un service rendu par quelqu'un d'autre.

parts.prompt: Write three sentences: a deduction in the past, a criticism with « should have », and a passive sentence about the shop.
parts.model: The thief must have known the shop was empty. Ms Ngo should have installed an alarm. The shop was broken into last night.
parts.explanation: Trois structures, trois phrases : vérifiez chaque participe passé.

exercises.prompt: « He ____ be tired : he has worked all day. »
The passive of « They are painting the school » is:
exercises.explanation: Present continuous passif : is being painted.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence has a causative meaning?
choices: My hair was cut off me by myself.
exercises.explanation: Have + objet + participe passé : on fait faire.

exercises.prompt: « You ____ have called me : I was worried. » (reproche)
exercises.explanation: Should have + pp exprime le reproche.
Après le passif impersonnel : infinitif avec to.
